doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Cello group, family and the road
title: Leaving Ventura, marriage and the amplified cello group
summary: After Ventura they marry and form a group with cello, guitar and bass that audiences are not ready for.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well after you left Ventura then did you decide to lead your own ensembles?
And that’s when we got married.

We wanted to — yeah we got married, that was pretty important, it was very nice. And we decided that we wanted to do something different because we didn’t want to go right back with tenor and the horns and everything. So I started a group with amplified cello

and guitar. Guitar would play tremulo to make sustained notes, and the bass would play arco. So those three, the cello and the bass and guitar, and the voices. Now that’s five lines, drums and piano. And it worked beautifully. And it was a wonderful sound, but no one was ready for it. So we had it about a year and a half and it was just like putting money into it, putting money into it, and—

I think part of the reason too is the fact that we started it and we weren’t that famous yet. I mean we had gotten a certain amount of notoriety with Charlie with the records, and we had a certain following, but we weren’t that well known. And when we first started with this group, we were working around Chicago and sort of in that area, and we were working strange clubs where people probably never heard of us, and saying what is this? And it was so unusual to see a cello playing jazz, and we had a girl who could improvise a little bit, and it was very interesting. The sound was wonderful, and we had fun doing it. We were the first ones to ever use the cello in a jazz group I believe.
Let’s see — who else used it after that? Chico Hamilton, right?
Yeah, Chico and there have been other people since, but I think it’s a great sound.
